prompt:
Design the floor plan of a low-poly science office for a three.js scene, in the style of a late-1990s PC game research facility. Write the plan as one JSON file named office-layout.json in the current directory. Write no other file. Reply with a short summary of the plan.

Frame (world units, right-handed, three.js axes):
- x runs to screen right, y runs up, z runs toward the viewer. The floor is at y = -2.2.
- A character stands in the room. His body is a box about 2.5 wide (x), 2.0 deep (z), and 3.1 tall. He never turns his back to the viewer.
- The desktop camera stands at [0, 0.75, 8.67], looks at [0, -0.35, -2.1], vertical field of view 44 degrees, aspect about 1.78.
- The phone camera stands at [0, 0.75, 6.93], same target, vertical field of view 50 degrees, aspect about 0.46. It sees only |x| < 1.5 at z = 0 and |x| < 2.4 at z = -4.
- The viewer can move the camera 1.4 units in x and z and can turn it all the way round. The camera can reach z = 13.7. The room must enclose that reach with 0.8 units to spare.
- A close shot frames his head from about 3 units in front of him, a little to one side.

Room:
- One rectangular room. The back wall is at about z = -4.5. Side walls at about x = -5.5 and x = 5.5. The front wall stands behind the camera. The ceiling is at about y = 2.4.
- The part of the room in front of z = 2 is the viewer's end. Keep it sparse: only items flat against the walls.

Props. Each prop is an axis-aligned box. Use these kinds, once each unless a count is given:
desk, monitor (a CRT on the desk), keyboard (on the desk), mug (on the desk), chair (office chair at the desk), whiteboard (on a wall), jar-shelf (a wall shelf or low cabinet that holds 5 specimen jars), jar (5 of them, on the jar-shelf, one is empty: mark it "empty": true), filing-cabinet (1 or 2), vending-machine or water-cooler (choose one or both), wall-clock (on a wall), door (in a wall), chamber-window (a wide window in a wall that looks into a test chamber, with a hazard-striped frame), ceiling-tube (4 to 6 fluorescent tubes on the ceiling, mark exactly one "flicker": true).

Composition. The phone is the main device, so plan the back of the room for the phone camera first:
- The phone sees only the band |x| < 2.4 of the back wall, and the character (2.5 wide) hides about half of that band wherever he stands. So build two stations against the back wall, one on each side of x = 0. When he stands at one side, the phone sees the other station.
- Left station, "the office": the desk stands against the back wall with its monitor, keyboard, and mug. The monitor and at least the right half of the desk lie inside -2.3 < x < -0.5. The chair is pulled out to the left of the desk, outside the walk. The whiteboard hangs on the back wall above the desk, its lower edge just above the monitor top, and at least half of it lies inside -2.4 < x < -0.4.
- Right station, "the science": the jar-shelf is a low cabinet against the back wall, and at least 3 of its 5 jars lie inside 0.5 < x < 2.4. The chamber-window is in the back wall above the jars, sill at about y = 0, top at about y = 1.9, about 4 wide, and at least half of it lies inside 0.2 < x < 2.4.
- The wall-clock hangs on the back wall near x = 0, high, between the whiteboard and the window.
- Side walls are seen only by the desktop camera, and only where z < 1. Left wall: filing cabinets. Right wall: the door (flat in the wall, between z = -3 and z = 0) and the vending machine or water cooler in front of it toward the viewer, z between 0.5 and 2.5.

Rules:
1. The character walks a loop of 4 stops. Back stops have |x| <= 0.9 and z about -1.2. Front stops have |x| <= 0.7 and z between 0.3 and 0.8. Stops alternate sides so he crosses the room. Each leg is at least 0.9 long.
2. Sweep his body box (2.5 wide by 2.0 deep) along every leg of the loop. Every prop that reaches below y = 1.2 must stay at least 0.5 units outside that swept area.
3. Nothing stands between either camera and the character: no prop with z > -2.6 may have |x| < 3.2, except ceiling tubes and items flat on the ceiling.
4. The monitor screen and the whiteboard face the viewer (+z).
5. The jars stand at about the character's chest height (y about -0.7 to 0.0).
6. Wall items are thin boxes (0.1 deep) placed 0.05 off the wall. Floor items rest on the floor (their bottom is at y = -2.2).
7. Sizes must be plausible next to the character: desk top about 1.25 above the floor, door about 3.6 tall and 1.7 wide, filing cabinet about 2.3 tall, vending machine about 3.3 tall, whiteboard about 3 wide and 1.7 tall, monitor about 0.8 cube, jars about 0.4 wide and 0.55 tall, mug about 0.25.
8. No two props may overlap, except that desk items rest on the desk top and jars rest on the jar-shelf. Wall items on the same wall must not overlap each other.
9. One stop stands near the jars, one near the desk, one under or near the flickering tube. He pauses 2.6 to 4.4 seconds at each stop.
10. Ceiling tubes run along z, lie over the walk area and the two stations (z between -4 and 2.5), and none hangs in front of the chamber window as seen from the cameras.

JSON shape:
{
  "room": { "minX": number, "maxX": number, "minZ": number, "maxZ": number, "floorY": -2.2, "ceilingY": number },
  "props": [
    { "id": string, "kind": string, "position": [x, y, z], "size": [width_x, height_y, depth_z], "facing": "+x" | "-x" | "+z" | "-z", "on": "floor" | "wall" | "ceiling" | "<id of the prop it rests on>", "note": string }
  ],
  "stops": [ { "position": [x, z], "near": string, "pauseSeconds": number } ],
  "cueTargets": { "jars": [x, y, z], "light": [x, y, z], "ceiling": [x, y, z] }
}
"position" is the centre of the box. "size" is the full extent along world x, y, z after the facing is applied. "facing" is the direction the front of the prop looks. "cueTargets.light" is the monitor screen or the chamber window. "cueTargets.ceiling" is the flickering tube.

Check your plan against every rule with arithmetic before you write the file. Use no names, logos, symbols, or text from any existing game or company. Write no readable text content anywhere in the plan.
purpose: Floor plan of the office set, as data. Codex wrote a JSON plan. The plan was then checked with checkOfficePlan and the mesh mascot's measured size.
changes: A first pass put the desk and the jars outside the band a phone sees. This prompt added the two stations on the back wall.

The keyboard moved back onto the desk top. The jars moved toward the front of the cabinet.
